severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — PROFESSIONAL SATURATION ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: MACHINE-WRITTEN FRONT ACHIEVES NEAR-HALF COVERAGE OF THE LINKEDIN PLATEAU AS NEW SURVEY DATA CONFIRMS EVERY OTHER LONG POST WAS WRITTEN BY NOBODY IN PARTICULAR
advisory: The National Slop Service has upgraded conditions across the professional interior to SEVERE following passive survey data indicating that roughly one in two long-form posts on the LinkedIn Plateau is now fully machine-generated. Residents are advised that a post reading 'I made a decision that changed everything' followed by three single-sentence paragraphs and a poll is not necessarily authored by a human, or, in fact, by anyone. The Service reminds the public that a comment reading 'This resonates deeply' is not confirmation of survivors. Shelter in place; do not engage.

regional_outlook.conditions: Total professional saturation. Machine-written thought pieces are settling at a rate of one every three seconds, each ending in the same rhetorical question aimed at no one. Visibility of actual humans reduced to near zero.
Secondary saturation band moving in from the Plateau. Automated reply columns forming rapidly, agreeing with everything and understanding nothing.
Cross-posted broetry runoff arriving in newsletter form. Expect the same three paragraphs you already scrolled past, now with a subject line that says 'A quick thought.'
Standing pools of 'top 7 lessons I learned' listicles. Waders recommended; solid ground scarce.
Calmer, with scattered engagement-bait polls. A drifting front of 'Type AMEN to agree' expected by late afternoon.

specimen.status: Explosively common; the dominant understory species of the LinkedIn Plateau
specimen.habitat: Comment sections beneath any post that received more than two other comments; migrates in flocks
specimen.field_marks: Appears within ninety seconds of publication. Praise is fulsome, generic, and structurally identical: an opening superlative, a restatement of the post's premise as though it were an insight, and a closing question inviting further engagement. Never disagrees. Never remembers.
specimen.call: So well said! Curious — how do you see this applying at scale in today's fast-moving landscape? 🙌
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuinely supportive colleague. Distinguish by asking a specific follow-up: a real colleague answers; the Synthetic Applause restates its compliment in a slightly warmer font and produces another emoji.

spotter_tip: If a 1,400-word post contains three separate one-word paragraphs — 'Then.' 'Everything.' 'Shifted.' — and closes by asking what YOU think, assume nobody thought anything. The em dash is not evidence either way, and yes, the Service is aware of the optics.
tomorrow: Continued heavy machine-written text over the Plateau, tapering to scattered thought leadership by evening; no meaningful clearing forecast.

confirmed_sighting.report: A study by AI-detection firm Pangram Labs, based on passive browsing data, found that nearly half of long-form LinkedIn posts are fully AI-generated, identifying the platform as the most AI-saturated of the major networks and noting that its years of built-in AI writing tools helped fuel the trend. Substack and X showed sharp rises as well.
